messages:
Maya: :rotating_light: noticing p99 latency spikes on streaming/generate across prod starting ~15:02 UTC. p95 rose from ~300ms to ~1.1s, p99 up to 7-9s, a few streaming stalls reported by clients. IncidentBot: Severity 2 alert triggered and page to #eng-oncall.

Maya: context — this started after a modest traffic ramp from a partner integration. No deploys in the last hour. Telemetry shows a sharp increase in KV cache eviction events and a jump in page-to-disk activity on several serving nodes.

Tomas: I can see the same metrics. KV cache hit rate dropped from 87% -> 55% on the high-traffic pool, and eviction counts spiked. Streaming stalls correlate with processes hitting GC/IO while paging.

Sawyer: grabbing logs from the affected hosts now. 

Sawyer: logs snippet from host-7: ```
[15:03:12] kv_cache: eviction triggered, freed=24MB, fragments=1123, policy=lrucap
[15:03:12] io: page_to_disk /mnt/kv/page-17 idx=3412 size=4MB
[15:03:13] decoder: prefill_enqueue request_id=rt-9a3, tokens=1024, prefill_size=1MB
[15:03:13] stream: stall detect request_id=rt-9a3 wait_ms=1200
```

Maya: those fragments number look bad — fragmentation + many small prefill writes causing IO pressure. Might be prefill vs decode imbalance: prefill large KV writes while decoders try to read.

Tomas: initial theory: under this traffic pattern the KV allocator is creating lots of small fragments. Eviction algorithm thrashes (evicting frequently) causing paging and IO contention which stalls decoder threads.

Jo: customer surface — two enterprise customers (acme-corp, nova-search) reported timeouts for streaming sessions around 15:05 UTC. CS is contacting them, flagged as potential SLA impact.

Maya: mitigation suggestions — short-term: reduce prefill aggressiveness, increase in-memory KV quota on hot pool, and enable an eviction backoff to avoid thrash. Also consider temporarily routing noisy tenant traffic to a fallback model instance without prefill caching.

Tomas: I can flip the prefill flag for the high-traffic route to "minimal" to prevent large prefill writes. Command to toggle feature flag (internal FF service):

```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $FF_TOKEN" \
  https://flags.internal/api/v1/toggle \
  -d '{"route":"/v1/streaming/generate","flag":"prefill_strategy","value":"minimal"}'
```

I'll run that now.

DeployBot: Feature flag change applied to route /v1/streaming/generate by Tomas.

Tomas: also bumping KV cache soft limit on pool `gpu-pool-3` from 48GB -> 64GB to reduce immediate evictions. Using runtime configmap patch:

```
kubectl -n runtime patch configmap runtime-config -p '{"data":{"gpu-pool-3.kv_soft_limit":"64G"}}'
kubectl -n runtime rollout restart daemonset/serving-worker
```

I'll restart workers in the pool one at a time to avoid disruption.

Sawyer: I'm launching a compacting job to defragment KV pages on affected hosts (non-blocking, low priority). Command:

```
/opt/redwood/bin/kv-compact --hosts host-3,host-7,host-9 --max-io=20MB/s
```

This will run over the next ~10m.

Maya: coordination — Tomas will apply FF + soft limit bump and sequential restart. Sawyer runs compact job. Jo will update CS and collect affected customer IDs. I'll monitor SLO panels and p99 traces.

Jo: reaching out to Acme & Nova now. Notifying them we're investigating root cause related to caching and IO; offering to route them to a stable region if needed.

(5m pass)

Tomas: prefill flag toggled to minimal and soft limit bumped on gpu-pool-3. Rolling restart in progress (1/6 done). Early metrics: eviction count down ~40% on restarted host, KV hit rate slowly improving.

Sawyer: compact job has started, no elevated IO beyond expected.

Maya: p95 has dropped back to ~420ms, p99 still elevated ~2.2s but trending down. Streaming stall events decreased from 14/min -> 3/min. Jo: customers acknowledged update, one asked for ETA — gave ~30m for stabilization.

Tomas: after 4/6 restarts, p99 is 1.1s and eviction rate near baseline. I recommend keeping prefill minimal for the next 2h while we run more diagnostic traces and plan a safer prefill strategy.

Sawyer: follow-up tasks I will create: 1) persistent compaction run overnight, 2) telemetry alert: fragmentation ratio > 0.25 -> page-down auto-scale, 3) patch eviction policy to add hysteresis.

Maya: decision: severity downgraded to S3. We're not seeing client impact beyond timeouts already reported. Keeping FF in minimal for 2h and KV soft limit at 64G for the pool.

Jo: CS updated both customers — they appreciate the quick response. Logging an incident ticket with timeline for them.

Maya: handoff — I'll sign out of pager in 10m. Tomas will own post-incident follow-ups (root cause investigation, prefill redesign, runbook updates). Sawyer will own compaction and eviction policy changes.

Sawyer: opening GH issues now and linking to runbook: https://git.internal/rw/serving/issues/987 — adding notes about fragmentation thresholds and mitigation playbook.

Tomas: adding an observability dashboard panel showing prefill write rate vs decode read latency and fragment count, plus an alert for echo state where eviction_count/time > 1000.

(1h later)

Maya: post-mortem stub: immediate cause = KV fragmentation + aggressive prefill writes under traffic spike -> eviction thrash -> paging -> decoder stalls -> latency spike. Mitigations applied: reduced prefill, bumped soft limits, started compaction.

Maya: current metrics stable, p95 ~330ms, p99 ~520ms, no new streaming stalls. Closing page but leaving follow-ups assigned. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
